title: Canonical total-fraction comparison for a flat finite birational algebra
statement: Let $A$ and $R$ be reduced commutative rings (having no nonzero nilpotent elements), and let $f:A\to R$ be flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For a ring $T$, let $Q(T)=S_T^{-1}T$, where $S_T$ consists of all non-zero-divisors $s$ (elements satisfying $sx=0\Rightarrow x=0$). Let $A\subseteq B\subseteq Q(A)$ be an $A$-subalgebra finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], put $C=B\otimes_A R$ [def-weil-module-base-change], and let $i:R\to C$ send $r$ to $1\otimes r$. Every $f(t)$ with $t\in S_A$ belongs to $S_R$, so $f$ extends uniquely to $\phi:Q(A)\to Q(R)$ with $\phi(a/t)=f(a)/f(t)$. The formula $$j(b\otimes r)=\phi(b)r$$ defines an injective $R$-algebra homomorphism $j:C\hookrightarrow Q(R)$, and $i$ is injective. More explicitly, for any finite $A$-generating family $b_h=a_h/t_h$ of $B$, with $a_h\in A$ and $t_h\in S_A$, put $s=\prod_ht_h$. Then $sB\subseteq A$, and multiplication by $f(s)$ is injective on $R$ and on $C$. The $A$-linear map $b\mapsto sb$ induces $d_R:C\to R$ with $d_R(b\otimes r)=f(sb)r$, satisfying $i(d_R(c))=f(s)c$ and $d_R(i(r))=f(s)r$. The image of $j$ lies in $R[1/f(s)]\subseteq Q(R)$, and $j(c)=d_R(c)/f(s)$. Identifying $R\subseteq C\subseteq Q(R)$ by these maps, $Q(C)$ is canonically isomorphic to $Q(R)$, compatibly with the maps from $C$; a fraction $c/t\in Q(C)$ maps to $(f(s)c)/(f(s)t)\in Q(R)$, with numerator and denominator in $R$ and the denominator a non-zero-divisor. If $C$ is integrally closed in $Q(C)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], then $j$ identifies $C$ with the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$.

source.place: Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion), proof: the finite integral normal algebra inside the localized base has to be its integral closure. Agent-explicit common-denominator and total-fraction calculation for arbitrary flat scalar extension, independent of completion.

proof.text: For any ring $T$, the map $T\to Q(T)$ is injective: if $x/1=0$, the fraction equivalence gives $ux=0$ for some $u\in S_T$, hence $x=0$. Fix $t\in S_A$. The injective $A$-linear map $A\xrightarrow{t}A$ stays injective after tensoring with the flat $A$-module $R$, by [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection]. Under $A\otimes_A R\simeq R$, $a\otimes r\mapsto f(a)r$, with inverse $r\mapsto1\otimes r$, it is multiplication by $f(t)$. Thus $f(t)\in S_R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] to $A\to R\to Q(R)$ and $S_A$ to obtain the unique $\phi$ with $\phi(a/t)=f(a)/f(t)$.

Choose the finite generating family in the statement. Products of regular elements are regular, since $uvx=0$ implies $vx=0$ and then $x=0$. Hence $s=\prod_h t_h\in S_A$. For each $h$, $sb_h=a_h\prod_{k\ne h}t_k\in A$. If $b=\sum_h e_hb_h$ with $e_h\in A$, then $sb=\sum_h e_h(sb_h)\in A$. This proves $sB\subseteq A$. Multiplication by $s$ on $B$ is injective because $s$ is a unit of $Q(A)$ and $B\subseteq Q(A)$. Write $\alpha=f(s)\in S_R$.

source.place: Tag 0518 (definition-finite-module), and explicit common-denominator calculation for varieties Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion)

proof.text: The injective $A$-linear map $d:B\to A$, $b\mapsto sb$, gives an injective base-changed map $d_R:C\to R$ by [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection], with $d_R(b\otimes r)=f(sb)r$. Applying the same leaf to the injective multiplication-by-$s$ map $B\to B$ shows that multiplication by $\alpha$ on $C$ is injective. On pure tensors, $i(d_R(b\otimes r))=1\otimes f(sb)r=(sb)\otimes r=\alpha(b\otimes r)$ and $d_R(i(r))=\alpha r$. Additivity gives both identities for all elements. If $i(r)=0$, the second identity and $\alpha\in S_R$ give $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), injection clause; base-change maps of Section 05G3 (section-base-change)

proof.text: The map $(b,r)\mapsto\phi(b)r$ is $A$-bilinear: the balancing identity is $\phi(ab)r=\phi(b)f(a)r$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] therefore defines $j:C\to Q(R)$. It sends $1\otimes1$ to $1$, is $R$-linear, and is multiplicative, since on two pure tensors both sides are $\phi(bb')rr'$; distributivity extends this to their finite sums. Thus $j$ is an $R$-algebra map and $ji(r)=r/1$. For a pure tensor, $\alpha j(b\otimes r)=\phi(sb)r=f(sb)r=d_R(b\otimes r)$, hence $j(c)=d_R(c)/\alpha$ for all $c$. This lies in $R[1/\alpha]$. If $j(c)=0$, injectivity of $R\to Q(R)$ gives $d_R(c)=0$, and injectivity of $d_R$ gives $c=0$.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product) and explicit multiplicativity/denominator calculation for varieties Tag 0C3V

proof.text: Identify $R\subseteq C\subseteq Q(R)$. Every $u\in S_R$ is regular on $C$: if $uc=0$, its image in $Q(R)$ is zero and $u$ is a unit there, so injectivity of $j$ gives $c=0$. Conversely let $t\in S_C$. The equality $\alpha t=i(d_R(t))$ puts $\alpha t$ in $R$. It is regular in $R$: if $(\alpha t)r=0$ for $r\in R$, the same equality in $C$ gives $t(\alpha r)=0$, hence $\alpha r=0$ by regularity of $t$ on $C$, and $r=0$ by regularity of $\alpha$ on $R$. Thus $j(t)=(\alpha t)/\alpha$ is a unit of $Q(R)$, with inverse $\alpha/(\alpha t)$.

source.place: Explicit regular-denominator calculation underlying varieties Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property], $j$ extends to $J:Q(C)\to Q(R)$, and $R\to C\to Q(C)$ extends to $H:Q(R)\to Q(C)$, using the two regularity conclusions of step 5. Their formulas give $J(c/t)=j(c)j(t)^{-1}=(\alpha c)/(\alpha t)$; both entries belong to $R$ and the denominator is regular there. The composite $JH$ is the identity by agreement on $R$ and localization uniqueness. For $c\in C$, $HJ(c/1)=H(d_R(c)/\alpha)=i(d_R(c))/i(\alpha)=\alpha c/\alpha=c/1$, because $\alpha$ is regular on $C$. Localization uniqueness applied to $C\to Q(C)$ then gives $HJ=1$. Thus $J$ is the canonical isomorphism, compatible with $C$, independently of the chosen generating family.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization); explicit inverse and fraction formula for varieties Tag 0C3V

proof.text: The elements $b_h\otimes1$ generate $C$ over $R$: for $b=\sum_h e_hb_h$, $b\otimes r=\sum_h(b_h\otimes1)f(e_h)r$, and pure tensors generate $C$. Hence $C$ is finite over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to $i:R\to C$: each $c\in C$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $R$. Applying $j$ to that equation shows $j(C)$ lies in the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$.

Assume $C$ is integrally closed in $Q(C)$. If $x\in Q(R)$ is integral over $R$, apply $H$ to its monic equation. The coefficients become elements of $i(R)\subseteq C$, so $H(x)$ is integral over $C$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and the assumed integral closedness, $H(x)=c/1$ for some $c\in C$. Therefore $x=JH(x)=j(c)$. Together with step 7 this identifies $j(C)$ with the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$, and all comparison, injectivity and denominator clauses have been proved.
